chunks: From him, from Musa ibn 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Sa'id al-Qammad, who said:

I heard a man ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who felt a pressing need in his stomach, or discomfort, or retention of urine, while he was in the obligatory prayer, in the first, second, third, or fourth rak'ah. He said: He said, 'If one of these occurs, there is no harm in him leaving to satisfy that need, performing ablution, then returning to the place where he was praying, and completing his prayer from the spot he left, provided he does not break the prayer with speech.'

I said, 'And if he turned to his right or left, or turned his back to the qibla?' He said, 'Yes, all of that is permissible; it is like the case of a man who made a mistake and turned back in one, two, or three rak'ahs of the obligatory prayer; he is only required to complete his prayer from where he left off.'
Then he mentioned the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) mistake. And the meaning of this report has already passed.

key_terms.سَهْوَ: Mistake or inadvertent error (referencing the Prophet's practice)
key_terms.عَصْراً: Retention or holding back of urine
key_terms.غَمْزاً: A pressing need or urge (specifically for urination)
key_terms.يَبْنِيَ عَلَى صَلَاتِهِ: To complete/build upon the prayer from the point of interruption

ai.seo_question: Can I leave my prayer to urinate and then resume it from where I left off?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the chapter on forgetfulness (sahw), establishing that minor physical needs do not invalidate the prayer's continuity if the worshipper returns to the same spot without speaking. The Imam clarifies that turning or looking around does not break the prayer, equating this state to the Prophet’s precedent of resuming prayer after a brief interruption for natural needs.
